lab.research.title: Research
lab.research.tagline: Public-safe research tracks — themes JasVerse is actively investigating with real evidence, not just an idea.
lab.research.card1.title: Cross-Platform Portability
lab.research.card1.desc: How to keep a product's build and behavior independent of any single operating system, device, or developer's machine — so nothing JasVerse ships silently depends on one laptop working correctly.
lab.research.card2.title: Mobile-First Product Delivery
lab.research.card2.desc: When and how a validated web product should become a mobile app — and how to make that a deliberate decision, not something that gets forgotten after launch.
lab.research.card3.title: Sandbox Continuity
lab.research.card3.desc: Making sure a test or staging environment can be understood and rebuilt by anyone with access to the code — not just the person who happened to set it up.
lab.research.card4.title: Zero-Budget Engineering
lab.research.card4.desc: Building real capability without paid services by default — preferring free, open, self-hostable tools, and only paying when there's a proven, material advantage.
lab.experiments.title: Experiments
lab.experiments.tagline: IDEA → RESEARCH → EXPERIMENT → VALIDATED → INTEGRATED (or ARCHIVED). Status is evidence-based, never aspirational.
lab.evidence.title: Evidence
lab.evidence.case.title: Case study: BBP Cross-Platform Build Portability
lab.evidence.case.problem: Problem: a filename/import case mismatch worked fine in the usual development environment, but failed on a different operating system.
lab.evidence.case.finding: Finding: a clean-room test — building the project from a fresh checkout, with no leftover local state — surfaced the failure immediately, where normal day-to-day development never would have.
lab.evidence.case.action: Action: the specific mismatch was fixed, and an automated check was added so the same class of problem can't silently return.
lab.evidence.case.result: Result: a portable, clean build — verified, not just assumed.
lab.method.title: Method
lab.method.tagline: The principles that are actually current — not aspirational marketing language.
lab.method.p1.title: Data Beats Claims
lab.method.p1.desc: Facts win over opinion. Something is verified by testing, reading real code, or checking a real system — not by how confidently it's described.
lab.method.p2.title: Web Validate → Mobile Deliver
lab.method.p2.desc: Prove a product matters on the web first. Mobile delivery is the default next step after real validation, not an afterthought.
lab.method.p3.title: Reuse Before Build
lab.method.p3.desc: Check whether something already exists before building it again under a new name.
lab.method.p4.title: Sandbox Before Risk
lab.method.p4.desc: Test in an isolated, disposable environment before touching anything real users depend on.
lab.method.p5.title: Zero-Budget First
lab.method.p5.desc: Free, open, and self-hostable by default. A paid tool is adopted only when it delivers a proven, material advantage.
lab.method.p6.title: Automate Repeated Human Work
lab.method.p6.desc: If the same manual task keeps repeating, that's a signal to build the automation, not to keep repeating it.
lab.method.p7.title: Production Over Meta-Work
lab.method.p7.desc: Governance, planning, and documentation exist to make real production better — never to replace it.
lab.method.note: These are operating principles, not a claim that any particular constitutional text is final — an unratified proposal is never presented here as adopted law.

pd.byebyeprice.whatItIs: An anti-scam price comparison engine: it pulls real listings from real sellers (eBay and affiliate networks) and surfaces an honesty signal on top of the raw price, instead of just the lowest number.
pd.byebyeprice.problem: Price-comparison sites are easy to game with manipulated "was" prices, hidden shipping costs, and fake discounts. Most comparison tools show whichever price is lowest without checking whether it's honest.
pd.byebyeprice.currentReality: Live and in active use at byebyeprice.com. It is real, working software with a production deployment, a daily price-snapshot pipeline and a real database of price history — not a mockup. It is still labeled BETA because it is actively evolving and has known open gaps (for example, data-freshness depends on a scheduled ingestion job that can lag).
pd.byebyeprice.capabilities: Real-time product search against live marketplace data · a "SafePrice" honesty score computed from actual price history (never fabricated when there isn't enough history to support it) · real-cost calculation including shipping · installable as a Progressive Web App on mobile.
pd.byebyeprice.whatExistsNow: A deployed web application and PWA, a production database of historical prices, and an automated ingestion pipeline.
pd.byebyeprice.whatDoesNotExistYet: No native Android or iOS app (no app-store listing of any kind). No verified public API for third parties.
pd.byebyeprice.currentNextStep: Continue hardening the existing web/PWA product before considering a native mobile wrapper (see Products for the ecosystem's web-first distribution approach).
pd.maikore.whatItIs: A voice-driven app-generation concept: speak a command describing an app, and get a working application deployed automatically, without writing code.
pd.maikore.problem: Building and deploying even a simple application still requires a developer. MaiKore's premise is to collapse "describe it" and "have it running" into one voice interaction.
pd.maikore.currentReality: Real, substantial code exists across the full stack — a FastAPI backend, a React web frontend, a React Native mobile app, and a defined pipeline (voice transcription → language-model planning → code generation → container build → Kubernetes deploy). It is not yet a working product a user can rely on: the pipeline depends on self-hosted GPU inference infrastructure that has not been provisioned, so end-to-end generation cannot run in production today.
pd.maikore.capabilities: Demo web and mobile clients exist with voice and typed input. The generation pipeline, authentication, and deployment orchestration are implemented in code but are not backed by live inference infrastructure.
pd.maikore.whatExistsNow: A complete application codebase (backend, web frontend, mobile app) and a demo-only web deployment.
pd.maikore.whatDoesNotExistYet: No provisioned production inference infrastructure (the GPU-backed language models the pipeline depends on). No published Android or iOS app.
pd.maikore.currentNextStep: Provision real inference infrastructure before any end-to-end generation claim can move from LAB to a working product.
pd.bosskey.whatItIs: A vision for one biometric key that replaces passwords and corporate logins, without Google or Facebook as gatekeepers.
pd.bosskey.problem: Identity online is largely mediated by a handful of corporate login providers. The Boss Key's premise is a single, user-owned biometric credential instead of that dependency.
pd.bosskey.currentReality: Currently a concept — no working implementation exists yet. This is a deliberately conservative classification, now formally registered in JasVerse's project registry as an EXPERIMENT with no engineering history for this idea, even though a public reference to the name has existed. Nothing here is inflated beyond what can be verified today.
pd.bosskey.capabilities: None yet — no code, no prototype, no demo.
pd.bosskey.whatExistsNow: The name and the underlying idea.
pd.bosskey.whatDoesNotExistYet: Everything else: no design spec, no prototype, no working software.
pd.bosskey.currentNextStep: No build work is planned. Any future work on this concept starts with JasVerse's Pre-Creation Gate, exactly like any other new asset.
